meta.title: Logical magic state distillation, 5-to-1

paper.authors: P. Sales Rodriguez, J. M. Robinson, P. N. Jepsen, Z. He et al. (QuEra, Harvard, MIT)
paper.title: Experimental demonstration of logical magic state distillation

meta.summary: Five magic states injected into color codes (d = 3 on 35 atoms, d = 5 on 85), then distilled by the 5-to-1 protocol with transversal gates: one logical magic state out, from 95.1% to 99.4% fidelity at d = 3 and 92.5% to 98.6% at d = 5.
meta.program: Two levels. The factory is the paper's circuit rebuilt from its Methods and figures: both injection encoders from the row-operation lists (R_ops) and the 5-to-1 circuit of Fig. 3a on whole rows of atoms (transversal gates), on the physical rows of Extended Data Fig. 1. The call is a logical program that consumes one magic state (`prepare |T>`: the `request_magic` system call) on a Steane block, which is the compiler's distance-3 color code, compiled against a machine whose factory is the d = 3 circuit on the twin.
meta.twin: The 17 × 5 grid of tweezer sites, one row per logical qubit. Global Raman rotations at 650 kHz and local ones at 250 kHz (the paper's Rabi frequencies), one global Rydberg pulse per CZ layer with the moving atoms 2 µm from their partners, a global echo with every move, imaging of every atom. RISC-Q at 500 MHz (on ZCU216 boards: one at d = 3, two at d = 5) drives one core per optical system and camera cores that threshold four atoms' counts each.
findings: The circuits check out against the paper: the d = 3 encoder of the Methods' row operations makes the [[7,1,3]] color code with exactly the |+⟩ qubits and injection qubit the Methods name, and the 24 operations of the d = 5 encoder make a distance-5 code for one assignment of initial states only, which the twin uses. Fig. 3a accepts the syndrome 1011 with probability exactly 1/6 for perfect inputs and returns the pure magic state; for slightly depolarized inputs the output error is quadratic in the input error.

On the twin every operation of both factories ran inside its window: the d = 3 factory takes 1.628 ms (35 atoms, six CZ layers of 139–233 µs each, dominated by AOD moves, then 500 µs of imaging) and the d = 5 factory 2.284 ms (85 atoms, eight CZ layers). Rotations, echoes and Rydberg pulses take about 13 µs of the 1.6 ms.

With the paper's stated error rates (gates, SPAM, T2) learned with Stim and applied to the exact five-qubit channel, the injected states come out at 96.5% (d = 3) and 96.1% (d = 5) after correction, against the paper's 95.1% and 92.5%; the distilled state at 99.8% for both, against 99.4% and 98.6%. The twin is better than the device, and more so at d = 5, which moves atoms more: the move-induced errors the paper does not quantify are the likely difference.
The factory accepts 5.2% of attempts at d = 3 and 0.70% at d = 5 with perfect stabilizers required on the four syndrome qubits (the ideal is 1/6).

As a system call: the compiler lowered a T gate on a Steane block (its d = 3 color code) against a machine whose factory is the d = 3 circuit (7 output and 28 workspace atoms, the paper's 35, and 1.628 ms), and its VM admitted the listing (RESOURCE_VALIDATED). The compiler refuses a factory whose output is not a whole block of the code: the base machine's 9-qubit factory was rejected for the 7-qubit block.

The interface's factory contract has a fixed latency and no acceptance probability. At the d = 3 factory's acceptance of 5.2%, a kept state takes 31 ms on average, 19 times what the compiler reserves: a factory with postselection needs a random-latency service in the system-call interface.
limits: The paper gives no durations of moves, Rydberg pulses, imaging or initialization. The twin uses the group's 2024 values (270 ns CZ, 500 µs imaging), Norcia et al. for optical pumping (100 µs), and a cited motion law (15 µs transfer, √(d/a) with a = 2750 m/s²) for moves; the pitch of 10 µm is the smallest the paper's 2 µm and 8 µm separations allow.
Move-induced dephasing is part of the paper's error model but its size is not given; it is left out, so the twin's fidelities are upper bounds of the model.
The CZ error is depolarizing; the paper's is biased towards Z and ZZ in proportions it does not give. Composite (amplitude-robust) pulse sequences are not published: a rotation takes its Rabi time.
The paper plays the first √Y layer as one global pulse. With the d = 5 encoder of its row operations, four atoms do not turn in that layer, so the twin drives it locally at d = 5.

Which atom of a pair moves, and whether moves avoid each other, is the twin's choice: the paper's search for move orders is not reproduced. Atom loss and the paper's sliding-scale postselection are not modeled.
The decoder is a sampled lookup table for both distances (the paper's MLD at d = 3; at d = 5 the paper uses a most-likely-error decoder).
The compiler has the d = 3 color code (Steane) built in but not the [[17,1,5]] code, so the system call is compiled for d = 3 only.

device.title: QuEra Gemini-class array, the 17 × 5 entanglement zone
device.basis: The circuit is rebuilt from the paper's Methods (row operations of both encoders) and Fig. 3a (distillation), and checked: both encoders produce the stated color codes, and Fig. 3a accepts 1/6 of perfect inputs with a pure magic state out. Rabi frequencies, fidelities, separations and the grid are the paper's. The paper gives no durations of moves, Rydberg pulses, imaging or initialization: they come from the group's 2024 paper and the cited motion law, as marked. Composite (amplitude-robust) pulse sequences are not published; a rotation takes its Rabi time. The controller is QuantumOS's RISC-Q model at 100 MHz.

call.programText:
code steane d=3

params  n

program[q: 1, c: 2]:
  prepare |T> -> ancilla[0]
  measure Z data[0] Z ancilla[0] -> c[0]
  measure X ancilla[0] -> c[1]
  when c[1]:
    frame Z data[0]
call.qecText:
codes:
  Steane [[7,1,3]]:
    stab    X[3]X[4]X[5]X[6]
    stab    X[1]X[2]X[5]X[6]
    stab    X[0]X[2]X[4]X[6]
    stab    Z[3]Z[4]Z[5]Z[6]
    stab    Z[1]Z[2]Z[5]Z[6]
    stab    Z[0]Z[2]Z[4]Z[6]
    logX[0] X[0]X[1]X[2]
    logZ[0] Z[0]Z[1]Z[2]
  merged1 = canonical_product base=Steane factors=1 requires=commuting_factors(P) blocks=distinct(family,block) n=sum(n)+1 k=sum(k)-rank(P_mod_base_checks) distance=unclaimed ancillas=1 checks=(base_checks,P*X[a],X[a]) check_signs=decoded_outcomes check_scope=(P*X[a],X[a]) check_prepare=|+> check_read=X split=Z
  merged2 = canonical_product base=Steane factors=2 requires=commuting_factors(P) blocks=distinct(family,block) n=sum(n)+1 k=sum(k)-rank(P_mod_base_checks) distance=unclaimed ancillas=1 checks=(base_checks,P*X[a],X[a]) check_signs=decoded_outcomes check_scope=(P*X[a],X[a]) check_prepare=|+> check_read=X split=Z

program[LogicData: 1, c: 54, ancilla: 68] (Steane[1] LogicData, Steane[1] LogicalAncilla):
  alloc LogicalAncilla[0,1)
  1 magic |T> -> LogicalAncilla[0,1)
  alloc ancilla[0,1)
  prepare |+> -> ancilla[0,1)
  alloc ancilla[1,7)
  merged2 LogicDataMerged0 = merge Z[LogicData[0][0]] Z[LogicalAncilla[0][0]] with ancilla[0,1) checks ancilla[1,7) -> c[0,6) commuting=proved
  extract LogicDataMerged0[0][0] rounds=3 using ancilla[7,43) -> syndrome[0,36)
  decode rounds=3 syndrome[0,36)
  decode rounds=3 c[0,6)
  Z[LogicData[0][0]] Z[LogicalAncilla[0][0]] = split LogicDataMerged0
  alloc ancilla[43,44)
  prepare |+> -> ancilla[43,44)
  alloc ancilla[44,50)
  merged1 LogicDataMerged1 = merge X[LogicalAncilla[0][0]] with ancilla[43,44) checks ancilla[44,50) -> c[6,12) commuting=proved
  extract LogicDataMerged1[0][0] rounds=3 using ancilla[50,68) -> syndrome[36,54)
  decode rounds=3 syndrome[36,54)
  decode rounds=3 c[6,12)
  X[LogicalAncilla[0][0]] = split LogicDataMerged1
  frame on c[10,12) Z[LogicData[0][0]]

verdictDetail.scope: Resource admission for the printed schedule: physical register bounds, compositional allocation/release identities, exclusive qubit use, machine capacities, and gadget/program upper budgets. Factory internals are the authored service contract. Conservative loop/call envelopes and all-taken guards. Does not certify quantum semantics, classical record causality/SSA, declarative protocol interfaces, lower bounds, or optimality.

protocol_findings.scope: Report only: rules this VM does not enforce; nothing here refuses and no other field depends on it. count: record bits, or gate executions; first_line: the least line of a counted finding. first: the first item of that line, null at count 0: line, unit (the gadget holding the line, or program), statement (the listing line without its time stamp, at most 240 bytes), callee (when the statement is a call); register, address, bits (the first offending cells in the listing's operand syntax reg[lo:hi], as the frame that counts them holds them: numbers at program scope, a loop's binder and a gadget's formals inside a body; for a gate its operands and qubits); operand (the statement's own clause that names the cells, as written); via (for cells of a statement inside a gadget that are counted at program scope: the program statement they came through, with its callee); port (for cells of a call's or loop's port: the whole port); inside (another statement the cells originate at, when the VM keeps it). bound exact: the program has no loop, guard, case or call and was compared cell by cell. gate_without_route (C4's rule of the staged compiler, on each frame's own statements): a two-qubit gate with no route statement of its frame that holds every operand, is complete by the gate's start and was not ended by a later route, allocation or release of one of its qubits or by a child that uses one; a frame's count times its calls and trips, guards as taken, the larger of alternatives; bound upper for this rule (a containment not shown counts); the compiler's local-rounds exemption is not applied. read_unwritten: cells a statement reads for which no write complete by the read is found among the other statements and children of its frame, nor of any enclosing frame up to the program; a loop's reads leave as the hull over its trips unless an earlier trip writes them. read_before_decode: the same for a value read (parity, frame update, guard) and a decode or a parity's output. Both bound upper under two conventions of this VM: a producer under a guard or in a case arm counts as run, and a producer port that is a hull (a loop whose trips leave gaps, a group of more than 4096 pieces) counts for all its cells; a cell written again keeps an earlier decode's credit. syndrome_never_decoded: cells of a syndrome write for which no decode input whose read is not before the write's completion is found among the other statements and children of its frame, nor of any enclosing frame up to the program (a loop's pending writes leave as the hull over its trips unless a later trip decodes them); bound upper under the same two conventions, a decode in place of a producer; a cell decoded and written again is counted. syndrome_bits_written, syndrome_bits_decoded: the syndrome bits that statements write and that decodes read, per execution (guards as taken, the larger of alternatives). record_overwrite: record bits outside source registers written by two statements or children of one frame (same address shape), or again by a later trip of a loop (stride below width), summed over walked frames times calls and trips (bound frame_sum: not a bound). record_rewritten_before_read: record bits (of source registers too) that are read (a value read or a decode's input) after something written LATER in the program has written the same cells again, so that the read sees that value and not the one the program had written before it. In a frame: the read's cells that a write (for a value read also a decode) of a later statement or child holds, of the same address shape and issued by the read's last time (the refusing checks make it complete by the first); not the cells that a statement before the reader produces in full after that producer is complete. In a loop whose trips have a period: per read port of the body the bits that later trips' write ports of the same address shape and stride have written again by the read's first time, over the trips that have such a later trip. Summed over walked frames times calls and trips (bound frame_sum: a child's port is a hull of cells with one time window, a child's read port counts its cells once whatever the number of reads behind it, and a guard counts as taken; writes and decodes are compared apart, so a later owner's write is not hidden by an earlier owner's decode that completes after it. Cells of different address shapes are not compared: pairs_not_compared counts the pairs of a read and a group of producers of another shape that the bounds do not show apart, in every frame walked, and above 0 the count may miss reads. By default the count is a rule (RECORD_REWRITTEN; --no-record-order only counts) and those pairs are decided: under an obligation checked where a gadget's formals are numbers, or by cutting the loops whose indices tell the shapes apart). would_refuse_require_specs: the first refusal the checks of --require-specs reach in this run, or null. comment_lines: lines of the listing holding #. untracked_ports above 0: record ports dropped where a site could not be moved or compared; the record counts may then miss reads. Null counts: the walk did not complete, or --bounds-only.

factory { output_qubits: 7 total, workspace_qubits: 28 total, latency: 1627790 ns, gates: 35 total, decoders: 1 total, classical_data_bandwidth: 1 bits/us, qubit_routing_bandwidth: 1 qubits/us }

max_parallel_gates.note: global pulses act on every atom

classical_data_bandwidth.note: board hub: one bit per batch at 100 MHz

qubit_routing_bandwidth.note: one AOD job moves every atom of a layer

gate1q_ns.note: a local Raman π/2 at 250 kHz

gate2q_ns.note: CNOT = two local rotations and the longest CZ layer (moves, Rydberg pulse, echo)

route_latency_ns.note: a route is the AOD move of a CZ layer

decoder_latency_ns.note: base machine value, rounded up to the 10 ns grid

pauli_frame_update_ns.note: base machine value, rounded up to the 10 ns grid

magic_state_latency_ns.note: the d = 3 factory on the Gemini twin

requestMagic.text: @100000 ns  ancilla[0:6] request_magic  state=|T>  with ancilla[7:34]

factory.note: One attempt of the factory takes the d = 3 circuit's time; it is kept for the accepted distillation syndrome and perfect stabilizers on the four syndrome qubits. The interface's factory contract has a fixed latency and no acceptance probability.

timingRefreshed: twin runs redone on the current controller model with each row's stored readout bits; noise statistics kept from the full run
